clue.text: Guess rightly that a popular song is being broadcast

parts.note: a hit is a song that tops the charts
a programme that is on is being transmitted

explanation.surface: Someone correctly names a chart song as it plays on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit on something is to stumble upon the correct idea or guess.

clue.text: Overlook a developed region

indicators.note: developed suggests the word region has been worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Planners neglect an area that has been built up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' shuffles REGION into the answer; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook something is to pay it no attention, to disregard it.

clue.text: Expelled alien roped up on a crossed bar

indicators.note: in a down clue, up tells us the word roped is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the letter T looks like a bar crossed by another, and is spelt out as tee

explanation.surface: A deported foreigner is tied to a cross-shaped bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ROPED into DEPOR; 'on' places TEE beneath it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A person expelled from a country as an unwanted foreigner is one deported.

clue.text: Counted on being given a reprimand

definitions.meaning: to tell off is an old sense of counting off one by one, as tellers count votes
scolded or rebuked by someone in authority

explanation.surface: Someone relied upon ends up scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' in its old sense of count survives in bank tellers and in telling off names on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Counted off in turn, and also scolded: two senses of the same phrase.

clue.text: Do one's utmost to get a football hooligan behind the posts

indicators.note: behind places the hooligan after the posts in the answer

parts.note: the goalposts make up a goal in football
a lout is a rough, aggressive young man

explanation.surface: Trying hard to catch a troublemaking fan who is lurking behind the goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert maximum effort, holding nothing back.

clue.text: At this point suffer depression in this mundane world

parts.note: here means at this place or moment
to be low is to feel depressed

explanation.surface: Feeling down at present amid earthly drudgery.
explanation.definitionFit: An old phrase for earthly life, as opposed to heaven above.

clue.text: The only one in a suit wearing underwear

definitions.text: The only one in a suit

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest worn under a shirt
clothes you have on are clothes you are wearing

explanation.surface: A man in a business suit is wearing a vest underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a card that is the only one held of its suit has a special name; 'suit' looks like clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games, a lone card held in a particular suit is so called.

clue.text: Why the matador may show embarrassment

definitions.text: Why the matador may show embarrassment

parts.words: Why the matador may show embarrassment
parts.note: read as two words, the phrase means turn crimson with shame, which a bullfighter would do after being horned by the bull

explanation.surface: A bullfighter blushes after a mishap in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as GO RED: to blush. A matador who has been pierced by the bull's horns might well do so.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador wounded by a bull's horn has been pierced, and that is also a blush split in two.

clue.text: A fish of the deep

definitions.meaning: a common edible sea and freshwater perch-like fish
low-pitched, as in the lowest singing voice

explanation.definitionFit: Both a familiar food fish and the lowest male vocal range.

clue.text: Fail as a philanthropist

parts.note: a benefactor's whole aim is to benefit others, so failing at it means achieving no benefit at all

explanation.surface: A charitable donor whose efforts come to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be of no benefit or use, the opposite of a philanthropist's purpose.

clue.text: A student told tales but made friends

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate
telling tales is telling untruths

explanation.surface: A pupil spread fibs yet still won companions.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined together as partners in a pact or friendship.

clue.text: Beat the unbeatable

definitions.meaning: to defeat or outdo someone
the finest, the one nobody can surpass

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to overcome; as a noun the top quality nobody can top.

clue.text: Make a lot of the trouble being finished

parts.note: a fuss is a commotion or bother
something over is ended

explanation.surface: The bother is finally done with.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper or give excessive attention to someone.

clue.text: Accept a role but break up

parts.note: to take something is to accept it
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: An actor agrees to a role and then goes to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle something into its components.

clue.text: A rotter meets his death by men carrying clubs

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, an old-fashioned rotter
to die is to meet one's death

explanation.surface: A villain is killed by men armed with cudgels.
explanation.walkthrough: The clubs are golf clubs, carried by the attendants on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf attendants carry a player's bag of clubs around the course.

clue.text: Leave by car to begin a game of golf

definitions.meaning: to depart in a vehicle

definitions.text: to begin a game of golf
definitions.meaning: the opening tee shot of a round

explanation.definitionFit: Both departing in a motor vehicle and making the first long golf stroke.

clue.text: Political group producing dramatised documentary

definitions.meaning: a dissenting clique within a party
a blend of fact and fiction in film or writing

explanation.definitionFit: Both a splinter group in a party and a genre mixing fact and fiction.

clue.text: No one is missing the point obviously!

definitions.text: No one is missing the point obviously!

parts.words: No one is missing the point obviously!
parts.note: read one way, the whole company is present; read another, someone sharp never misses the point because they are mentally alert

explanation.surface: A roll call finds everyone present, and everyone gets the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both fully present and mentally sharp.

clue.text: Elegant recidivist made to pay for his crime

definitions.meaning: cultivated and polished in manner

definitions.text: recidivist made to pay for his crime
definitions.meaning: a repeat offender penalised again would be fined once more

explanation.definitionFit: Polished and cultured, and also punished with a fine a second time.

clue.text: Sapper likely to be dependable

parts.note: a sapper is a soldier in the Royal Engineers, RE
liable means likely to do something

explanation.surface: A military engineer who can be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: Trustworthy and consistently to be counted on.

clue.text: Popular BBC comeback

indicators.note: comeback means the word reads the same when read in the return direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: The British broadcaster stages a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: The nickname reads identically in both directions, so it comes back as itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal nickname the British public uses for the national broadcaster.

clue.text: Extol a martyred archbishop

definitions.meaning: to praise highly
William ..., Archbishop of Canterbury, executed in 1645

explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb for praising and the name of an executed Archbishop of Canterbury.

clue.text: Completely finished though not even started

definitions.meaning: ruined, brought to destruction
a job left not done

explanation.definitionFit: Both ruined and left unperformed: two opposite senses.

clue.text: Finish with one's tail in the air

definitions.meaning: to land up somewhere eventually

definitions.text: with one's tail in the air
definitions.meaning: the rear end upward, as a phrase read literally

explanation.definitionFit: To arrive finally somewhere, and also a rear raised high.

clue.text: A bit given to each one

parts.note: a piece is a bit or portion

explanation.definitionFit: Each, for every individual person or item.

clue.text: Like a fugitive not out to get a beating

parts.note: a batsman not out in cricket is still in
a hiding is a thrashing

explanation.surface: An escapee risks a thrashing if caught.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who is not out is said to be in.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive conceals themselves from the authorities.

clue.text: Trade vessel

definitions.meaning: a skilled occupation or handicraft
a boat or ship

explanation.definitionFit: Both a skilled occupation and a boat.

clue.text: Young princess has to telephone when overcoming depression

parts.note: Bea is short for Princess Beatrice
to ring up is to phone

explanation.surface: A royal girl phones someone during a low patch.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Beatrice, granddaughter of Queen Elizabeth II, is familiarly Bea.
explanation.definitionFit: Coping cheerfully under strain or misfortune.
